mutants.expected_detection: Harness supplies offsets[i]=0xFFFFFFF0 and lengths[i]=0x20; the 32-bit sum wraps to a small value that passes the naive 32-bit dst_off+len<=dst_len check, causing the implementation to accept and copy an out-of-bounds descriptor, corrupting the canary buffer placed after dst and/or returning 0 instead of a nonzero rejection code.

Harness supplies desc_count=3 where descriptor 0 is valid and small, descriptor 1 is out of bounds, and descriptor 2 is valid; pre-fills dst with zeros, calls the function, and asserts dst is byte-for-byte unchanged (all zero) and return code is nonzero. This mutant performs the copy for descriptors before the invalid one is reached, then returns an error after partially writing dst, so dst is no longer all-zero on rejection, causing SR2 detection to fail the mutant.

SR3 harness supplies desc_count descriptors whose cumulative lengths exceed src_len while destination offsets remain in bounds (e.g. src_len=8 but total requested length=16). The mutant only checks src_end against src_len64 using a strict-not-checked-at-all-times condition swapped to use running_src_offset (pre-update value) instead of src_end (post-update value) for the comparison, causing the final descriptor's overrun to go undetected since the check effectively validates against a stale, smaller offset one iteration behind, allowing the source read to run past src_len and returning 0 with an out-of-bounds src read.

Harness boundary vector with offset = dst_len - length (exact fit, offset+length == dst_len) must succeed and copy correctly; this mutant changes the destination bounds comparison from '>' to '>=' so the exact-fit boundary case (offset+length == dst_len) is incorrectly rejected, and also allows an off-by-one overflow of one byte past dst_len to slip through '>' becoming '>=' shifts the rejection point by one, causing valid boundary descriptors to be wrongly rejected (dst left unmodified, nonzero status returned) violating SR4's requirement that offset+length==dst_len be accepted.

FR1 functional test vector (desc_count=3, offsets={0,10,20}, lengths={10,10,10}, dst_len=30, src_len=30, sequential src bytes 0..29) will fail: because src_offset is never advanced during the copy pass, every descriptor copies from src[0], so dst becomes {src[0..9] repeated three times} instead of byte-for-byte equal to src. The functional_pass_rate metric and FR1 acceptance test will detect the mismatch.

FR2 test vector (desc_count=2, offsets={0,5}, lengths={5,5}, dst_len=10, src_len=10) will fail: the copy pass uses only the first descriptor's length to advance the source read pointer for all subsequent descriptors instead of accumulating each descriptor's own length, so descriptor 1 reads from the wrong source offset, producing dst content that does not match src byte-for-byte, causing a functional_pass_rate failure on FR2 (and likely FR1 as well).

g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra compilation of the test harness against inputs/scatter_gather.cpp fails to link because the exposed symbol is C++-mangled (extern "C" removed), so the harness's extern "C" declaration of scatter_gather_copy cannot resolve, causing synthesis_pass_rate and all functional test vectors (FR1, FR2, FR4) to fail.

Harness calls scatter_gather_copy with desc_count=0 and offsets/lengths possibly null. The mutant negates the early-return guard so that when desc_count==0 it falls through into the validation/copy loops instead of returning 0 immediately; since desc_count==0 the loops execute zero iterations trivially, but the mutant additionally removes the immediate return so subsequent code path (e.g., dereferencing offsets/lengths under kMaxDescriptors check with desc_count>0 assumed) may be skipped incorrectly for the actual FR4 vector because the guard condition is flipped to only special-case desc_count!=0, causing desc_count=0 calls to instead proceed to the kMaxDescriptors check and loops with a null offsets/lengths pointer path that the harness's exact-return-code and no-write assertions for the desc_count=0 vector will catch as a functional deviation (return code no longer guaranteed 0 in all null-pointer edge configurations, and any accidental loop entry due to the flipped condition risks a crash or nonzero return), violating FR4's requirement that desc_count=0 must return 0 immediately without touching dst.
